new.md:
Creates a new `GtkButton` widget.

To add a child widget to the button, use [`Button.set_child()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#method:set_child).

new_from_icon_name.brief: Creates a new button containing an icon from the current icon theme.
new_from_icon_name.md:
Creates a new button containing an icon from the current icon theme.

If the icon name isn’t known, a “broken image” icon will be
displayed instead. If the current icon theme is changed, the icon
will be updated appropriately.

new_with_label.brief: Creates a `GtkButton` widget with a `GtkLabel` child.
new_with_label.md: Creates a `GtkButton` widget with a `GtkLabel` child.

new_with_mnemonic.brief: Creates a new `GtkButton` containing a label.
new_with_mnemonic.md:
Creates a new `GtkButton` containing a label.

If characters in `label` are preceded by an underscore, they are underlined.
If you need a literal underscore character in a label, use “__” (two
underscores). The first underlined character represents a keyboard
accelerator called a mnemonic. Pressing <kbd>Alt</kbd> and that key
activates the button.

doc.brief: Calls a callback function when the button is clicked.
doc.md:
Calls a callback function when the button is clicked.

The `GtkButton` widget can hold any valid child widget. That is, it can hold
almost any other standard `GtkWidget`. The most commonly used child is the
`GtkLabel`.

# Shortcuts and Gestures

The following signals have default keybindings:

- [`Button::activate`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#event:activate)

# CSS nodes

`GtkButton` has a single CSS node with name button. The node will get the
style classes .image-button or .text-button, if the content is just an
image or label, respectively. It may also receive the .flat style class.
When activating a button via the keyboard, the button will temporarily
gain the .keyboard-activating style class.

Other style classes that are commonly used with `GtkButton` include
.suggested-action and .destructive-action. In special cases, buttons
can be made round by adding the .circular style class.

Button-like widgets like [`ToggleButton`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ToggleButton), [`MenuButton`](xref:gtk:Gtk.MenuButton),
[`VolumeButton`](xref:gtk:Gtk.VolumeButton), [`LockButton`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LockButton), [`ColorButton`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorButton)
or [`FontButton`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FontButton) use style classes such as .toggle, .popup, .scale,
.lock, .color on the button node to differentiate themselves from a plain
`GtkButton`.

# Accessibility

`GtkButton` uses the [`AccessibleRole.button`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:button) role.

get_can_shrink.brief: Retrieves whether the button can be smaller than the natural size of its contents.
get_can_shrink.md:
Retrieves whether the button can be smaller than the natural
size of its contents.

get_has_frame.brief: Returns whether the button has a frame.
get_has_frame.md: Returns whether the button has a frame.

get_icon_name.brief: Returns the icon name of the button.
get_icon_name.md:
Returns the icon name of the button.

If the icon name has not been set with [`Button.set_icon_name()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#method:set_icon_name)
the return value will be `NULL`. This will be the case if you create
an empty button with [`Button.new()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#constructor:new) to use as a container.

get_label.brief: Fetches the text from the label of the button.
get_label.md:
Fetches the text from the label of the button.

If the label text has not been set with [`Button.set_label()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#method:set_label)
the return value will be `NULL`. This will be the case if you create
an empty button with [`Button.new()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#constructor:new) to use as a container.

get_use_underline.brief: gets whether underlines are interpreted as mnemonics.
get_use_underline.md:
gets whether underlines are interpreted as mnemonics.

See [`Button.set_use_underline()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#method:set_use_underline).

set_can_shrink.brief: Sets whether the button size can be smaller than the natural size of its contents.
set_can_shrink.md:
Sets whether the button size can be smaller than the natural size of
its contents.

For text buttons, setting `can_shrink` to true will ellipsize the label.

For icons and custom children, this function has no effect.

set_child.md:
Sets the child widget of `button`.

Note that by using this API, you take full responsibility for setting
up the proper accessibility label and description information for `button`.
Most likely, you'll either set the accessibility label or description
for `button` explicitly, or you'll set a labelled-by or described-by
relations from `child` to `button`.

set_has_frame.brief: Sets the style of the button.
set_has_frame.md:
Sets the style of the button.

Buttons can have a flat appearance or have a frame drawn around them.

set_icon_name.brief: Adds a `GtkImage` with the given icon name as a child.
set_icon_name.md:
Adds a `GtkImage` with the given icon name as a child.

If `button` already contains a child widget, that child widget will
be removed and replaced with the image.

set_label.brief: Sets the text of the label of the button to `label`.
set_label.md:
Sets the text of the label of the button to `label`.

This will also clear any previously set labels.

set_use_underline.brief: Sets whether to use underlines as mnemonics.
set_use_underline.md:
Sets whether to use underlines as mnemonics.

If true, an underline in the text of the button label indicates
the next character should be used for the mnemonic accelerator key.

can-shrink.brief: Whether the size of the button can be made smaller than the natural size of its contents.
can-shrink.md:
Whether the size of the button can be made smaller than the natural
size of its contents.

For text buttons, setting this property will allow ellipsizing the label.

If the contents of a button are an icon or a custom widget, setting this
property has no effect.

has-frame.brief: Whether the button has a frame.
has-frame.md: Whether the button has a frame.

icon-name.brief: The name of the icon used to automatically populate the button.
icon-name.md: The name of the icon used to automatically populate the button.

label.brief: Text of the label inside the button, if the button contains a label widget.
label.md: Text of the label inside the button, if the button contains a label widget.

use-underline.brief: If set, an underline in the text indicates that the following character is to be used as mnemonic.
use-underline.md:
If set, an underline in the text indicates that the following character is
to be used as mnemonic.

activate.brief: Emitted to animate press then release.
activate.md:
Emitted to animate press then release.

This is an action signal. Applications should never connect
to this signal, but use the [`Button::clicked`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Button#event:clicked) signal.

The default bindings for this signal are all forms of the
<kbd>␣</kbd> and <kbd>Enter</kbd> keys.

clicked.brief: Emitted when the button has been activated (pressed and released).
clicked.md: Emitted when the button has been activated (pressed and released).

activate.brief: Signal that causes the button to animate press then release.
activate.md:
Signal that causes the button to animate press then
   release. Applications should never connect to this signal, but use
   the `clicked` signal.

clicked.brief: Signal emitted when the button has been activated (pressed and released).
clicked.md: Signal emitted when the button has been activated (pressed and released).
